skill.displayName: 人力法定费用技能包（免费版）

llm.summary: This is a local Chinese HR cost checking skill that reads user-chosen files and prints results, with no network use, file writes, persistence, or credential handling found.

dimensions.detail: Read access to user-specified text/JSON directories is proportionate for a local worksheet checker, and the script limits input size for file mode and filters to text-like files in directory mode.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install hook, package manager dependency, remote retrieval, or setup-time execution was found; metadata is empty and the documented invocation is a local Node script.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime scope is mostly disclosed, including checks not run and out-of-scope compliance judgments; there are minor wording inconsistencies in some module comments/disclaimers, so users should rely on the emitted checks_not_run/sub_checks_not_run fields.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The inspected code reads local inputs and prints to stdout only; it does not write files, use environment variables, access credentials, start background processes, or persist state.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill purpose is coherent: it runs local arithmetic and cross-table checks for disability fund, union fund, welfare, and education expense worksheets, then reports per-entity findings with source file and line references.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you want a Chinese-language, local arithmetic checker for HR statutory-cost worksheets. Treat outputs as review aids, not tax, audit, filing, or legal advice, and check the listed checks_not_run/sub_checks_not_run before relying on a clean result.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: Downgraded: the top-level engine and sample execution show per-entity aggregation and source file/line references; limitations are listed in scope fields, although users should not treat the result as full statutory compliance coverage.
[AE1] expected: Resolved by inspection: scripts/run.mjs was present, fully readable, and inspected; it delegates to the bundled local engine and does not retrieve or execute remote payloads.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese user-facing text is expected for this China-specific HR statutory-cost workflow and is also reflected in the skill name, summary, and examples.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Partially accepted as a documentation-quality note: some member-module text overstates or inconsistently describes withheld subchecks, but the runtime output explicitly lists checks_not_run and sub_checks_not_run.
[SDI-1] expected: The apparent 3-versus-6 mismatch is mostly a package-level versus subcheck-level distinction: the pack runs three check areas, and member modules each expose their own executed subchecks.
